title: The V9938 VDP control, command and status registers
covers: The write-only control registers R#0 to R#23 and the command registers R#32 to R#46 of the Yamaha V9938, and the read-only status registers S#0 to S#9 read from the same port, with each bit the data book defines

rows.text: Register 0 is mode register 0: bit 7 and bit 0 read 0, and bits 6 to 1 are DG, IE2, IE1, M5, M4 and M3.
DG sets the color bus to input mode and inputs data into the VRAM.
IE2 enables the light pen interrupt.
IE1 enables the interrupt from a horizontal scanning line.
M5, M4 and M3 change the display mode.
A write to register 0 keeps bits 1 to 6 of the value, the bits the data book names, and drops bits 7 and 0.
MAME's register-0 case stores the value, recomputes the mode and the interrupt line, and does nothing for bit 6: the color bus is neither switched nor fed.
MAME's register-0 case stores the value, recomputes the mode and the interrupt line, and does nothing for bit 5: no light pen interrupt is armed.
MAME aborts a running command and clears bit 0 of S#2 when the mode changes; the data book leaves that case open.
MAME looks the mode number up in a table of named modes, each with its own entry, and stops at the row holding 0xff, the UNKNOWN mode.
Register 1 is mode register 1: bit 7 and bit 2 read 0, and bits 6 to 0 are BL, IE0, M1, M2, SI and MAG.
BL enables the screen display when 1 and disables it when 0.
IE0 enables the interrupt from a horizontal scanning line.
MAME gates bit 7 of S#0, its vertical scanning flag, with IE0, not a horizontal one; S#1 bit 0 is the flag it reads with IE1.
M1 and M2 change the display mode.
SI sets the sprite size: 16 by 16 when 1, 8 by 8 when 0.
MA expands the sprites when 1 and leaves them normal when 0.
A write to register 1 sets the six bits its line names: BL, IE0, M1, M2, SI and MAG.
Register 8 is mode register 2: MS, LP, TP, CB, VR, a 0 bit, SPD and BW, from bit 7 to bit 0.
MS sets the color bus to input mode and enables the mouse when 1, and output mode without the mouse when 0.
LP enables the light pen when 1 and disables it when 0.
TP sets the color of code 0 to the color of the palette.
CB sets the color bus to input mode when 1 and output mode when 0.
VR selects the type of Video RAM: 64K by 1 or 64K by 4 bits when 1, 16K when 0.
SPD disables the display of sprites when 1 and shows them when 0.
BW selects black and white in 32 tones when 1 and color when 0, which needs a composite encoder.
A write to register 8 sets the seven bits its line names: MS, LP, TP, CB, VR, SPD and BW.
Register 9 is mode register 3: LN, a 0 bit, S1, S0, IL, EO, *NT and DC, from bit 7 to bit 0.
LN sets the horizontal dot count to 212 when 1 and to 192 when 0.
S1 and S0 select the simultaneous mode.
IL selects interlace with complete NTSC timing when 1, and non-interlace when 0.
EO alternately displays two graphic screens by even and odd field when 1.
NT, drawn with a bar and for RGB output only, selects PAL with 313 lines when 1 and NTSC with 262 when 0.
DC sets the DLCLK pin to input mode when 1 and output mode when 0.
A write to register 9 sets the seven bits its line names: LN, S1, S0, IL, EO, NT and DC.
MAME recomputes the horizontal offset from R#18 whenever R#9 is written, coupling the two registers in one path.
Register 2 is the pattern name table base address register: bit 7 is 0 and bits 6 to 0 are A16 to A10.
Register 2 holds the high seven bits, A16 to A10, of the pattern name table base address.
Register 3 is the low register of the color table base address: its eight bits are A13 to A6.
Register 3 holds A13 to A6 of the color table base address.
Register 10 is the high register of the color table base address: bits 7 to 3 are 0 and bits 2 to 0 are A16 to A14.
Register 10 holds A16 to A14 of the color table base address.
The capture draws register 4 with five 0 bits and then A16, A15 and A14 in bits 2 to 0.
A write to register 4 holds the pattern generator table base address bits its line names, A16 to A14.
MAME masks register 4 with 0x3f, keeping bits 5 to 0, so it keeps the three bits the capture draws as 0.
Register 5 is the low register of the sprite attribute table base address: its eight bits are A14 to A7.
Register 5 holds A14 to A7 of the sprite attribute table base address.
Register 11 is the high register of the sprite attribute table base address: bits 7 to 2 are 0 and bits 1 and 0 are A16 and A15.
Register 11 holds A16 and A15 of the sprite attribute table base address.
Register 6's line gives bits 7 and 6 as 0 and bits 5 to 0 as A16 to A11.
The capture titles register 6 the sprite attribute table base address register high.
A write to register 6 holds A16 to A11, the six address bits its line gives.
Register 7 is the text color and backdrop color register: bits 7 to 4 are TC3 to TC0 and bits 3 to 0 are BD3 to BD0.
TC3 to TC0 specify the text color in the TEXT 1 and TEXT 2 modes.
BD3 to BD0 specify the backdrop color in every display mode.
A write to register 7 sets the text color in its high four bits and the backdrop color in its low four bits.
Register 12 is the text color and back color register: bits 7 to 4 are T23 to T20 and bits 3 to 0 are BC3 to BC0.
T23 to T20 specify the color of part 1 of the pattern.
BC3 to BC0 specify the color of part 0 of the pattern.
In the TEXT 2 mode, where the attributes ask for blinking, the color of this register and the one of R#7 alternate.
A write to register 12 sets the two pattern colors and, in TEXT 2 with blinking, the color shown alternately with R#7.
Register 13 is the blinking period register: bits 7 to 4 are ON3 to ON0 and bits 3 to 0 are OF3 to OF0.
In GRAPHIC 4 to GRAPHIC 7 the two pages alternate; this register sets the page the blinking starts on and is also used in TEXT 2.
ON3 to ON0 are the display time of the even page.
OF3 to OF0 are the display time of the odd page.
A write to register 13 sets the display time of the even page and of the odd page.
Register 14 is the VRAM access base address register: bits 7 to 3 are 0 and bits 2 to 0 are A16 to A14.
When the MSX-VIDEO and the VRAM are accessed, the high-order three bits of the address are set in this register.
A carry from A13 increments the register, except in GRAPHIC 1, GRAPHIC 2, MULTICOLOR and TEXT 1 modes, where it is not incremented.
A write to register 14 sets the high bits of the address the VRAM access uses.
Register 15 is the status register pointer: bits 7 to 4 are 0 and bits 3 to 0 are S3 to S0.
A read of the status registers S#0 to S#9 answers the one this pointer names.
A write to register 15 sets the number of the status register a read returns.
MAME drops a pending palette write pair when R#15 is written with a value it does not already hold.
Register 16 is the color palette address register: bits 7 to 4 are 0 and bits 3 to 0 are C3 to C0.
When setting a color palette, the number of the palette entry is set in this register.
A write to register 16 sets the palette entry number.
Register 17 is the control register pointer: bit 7 is AII, bit 6 is 0 and bits 5 to 0 are RS5 to RS0.
The pointer may be used to access another register, and the AII bit says whether the data is automatically incremented.
AII = 1 disables the auto increment and AII = 0 enables it.
A write to register 17 sets the register number the indirect write uses and the auto increment bit.
Register 18 is the display adjust register: bits 7 to 4 are V3 to V0 and bits 3 to 0 are H3 to H0.
The register adjusts the display position on the CRT.
H runs from 7 down to 1 at the left, 0 at the center and 15 down to 8 at the right.
V runs from 8 up to 15 at the bottom, 0 at the center and 1 up to 7 at the top.
A write to register 18 sets the horizontal adjustment, H3 to H0, of the display position.
MAME takes the vertical adjustment from the high nibble of R#18 once per frame, not on the write, which reaches only the horizontal one.
Register 19 is the interrupt line register: its eight bits are IL7 to IL0.
It sets the scanning line at which the MSX-VIDEO interrupts, once the interrupt is enabled.
A write to register 19 sets the number of the scanning line that raises the interrupt.
Register 20 is color burst register 1, whose eight bits are 0.
The value is preset when power is applied; setting all three color burst registers to 0 erases the color burst of the composite output.
A write to register 20 sets color burst register 1.
MAME logs that the color burst registers are not emulated, so a write to this one produces no signal.
Register 21 is color burst register 2, drawn with the value 00111111.
A write to register 21 sets color burst register 2.
MAME logs that the color burst registers are not emulated, so a write to this one produces no signal.
Register 22 is color burst register 3, drawn with the value 00000101.
A write to register 22 sets color burst register 3.
MAME logs that the color burst registers are not emulated, so a write to this one produces no signal.
Register 23 is the display offset register: its eight bits are DO7 to DO0.
The register sets the line of the VRAM at which the display begins.
A write to register 23 sets the first line of the VRAM that the display shows.
Register 32 is the source X low register; its eight bits are SX7 to SX0.
A write to register 32 sets the low eight bits of the source X coordinate.
Register 33 is the source X high register: bits 7 to 1 are 0 and bit 0 is SX8.
A write to register 33 sets the ninth bit, SX8, of the source X coordinate.
Register 34 is the source Y low register; its eight bits are SY7 to SY0.
A write to register 34 sets the low eight bits of the source Y coordinate.
Register 35 is the source Y high register: bits 7 to 2 are 0 and bits 1 and 0 are SY9 and SY8.
A write to register 35 sets the two high bits, SY9 and SY8, of the source Y coordinate.
Register 36 is the destination X low register; its eight bits are DX7 to DX0.
A write to register 36 sets the low eight bits of the destination X coordinate.
Register 37 is the destination X high register: bits 7 to 1 are 0 and bit 0 is DX8.
A write to register 37 sets the ninth bit, DX8, of the destination X coordinate.
Register 38 is the destination Y low register; its eight bits are DY7 to DY0.
A write to register 38 sets the low eight bits of the destination Y coordinate.
Register 39 is the destination Y high register: bits 7 to 2 are 0 and bits 1 and 0 are DY9 and DY8.
A write to register 39 sets the two high bits, DY9 and DY8, of the destination Y coordinate.

entries.name: R40 number of dots X low

rows.text: Register 40 is the number of dots X low register; its eight bits are NX7 to NX0.
A write to register 40 sets the low eight bits of the number of dots on the X axis.
Register 41 is the number of dots X high register: bits 7 to 1 are 0 and bit 0 is NX8.
A write to register 41 sets the ninth bit, NX8, of the number of dots on the X axis.

entries.name: R42 number of dots Y low

rows.text: Register 42 is the number of dots Y low register; its eight bits are NY7 to NY0.
A write to register 42 sets the low eight bits of the number of dots on the Y axis.
Register 43 is the number of dots Y high register: bits 7 to 2 are 0 and bits 1 and 0 are NY9 and NY8.
A write to register 43 sets the two high bits, NY9 and NY8, of the number of dots on the Y axis.
Register 44 is the color register: bits 7 to 4 are CH3 to CH0 and bits 3 to 0 are CL3 to CL0.
A write to register 44 sets the color register, bits CH3 to CH0 and CL3 to CL0.
MAME passes the value to its command unit, which keeps it as its own CL, and the VRAM to CPU command reads it back.
Register 45 is the argument register: bit 7 is 0 and bits 6 to 0 are MXC, MXD, MXS, DIY, DIX, EQ and MAJ.
A write to register 45 sets the argument register: MXC, MXD, MXS, DIY, DIX, EQ and MAJ.
Register 46 is the command register: bits 7 to 4 are CM3 to CM0 and bits 3 to 0 are LO3 to LO0.
A write to register 46 sets the command register: CM3 to CM0 and LO3 to LO0.
MAME takes bits 7 to 4 as the command and bits 3 to 0 as the logical operation, and does nothing outside GRAPHIC 4 to GRAPHIC 7.
Status register 0 holds F in bit 7, 5S in bit 6, C in bit 5 and the fifth sprite number in bits 4 to 0.
F is the vertical scanning interrupt flag, and it is reset when S#0 is read.
5S reports that five sprites, or nine in G3 to G7, are aligned on the first horizontal line.
C reports that two sprites have collided.
Bits 4 to 0 hold the number of the fifth, or ninth, sprite.
Reading S#0 returns the four fields and resets the F flag.
MAME raises F at the vertical blanking and sets 5S and the sprite number in its sprite pass.
MAME clears bits 6 and 5 of S#0, the fifth sprite and collision flags, as well as bit 7 when the register is read.
Status register 1 holds FL, LPS, the identification number, FH, and, with a mouse, the two mouse switches.
FL is the light pen flag; it and IE2 must both be set for an interrupt, and a read of S#1 resets it.
With a mouse, bit 7 reports its second switch, and a read of S#1 does not reset it.
LPS reports that the light pen switch was pressed and is not reset by a read.
With a mouse, bit 6 reports its first switch, and a read of S#1 does not reset it.
The identification number names the chip; the transcription's editor's note gives 0 for the V9938, 1 for the V9948 and 2 for the V9958.
FH is the horizontal scanning interrupt flag of the line set in R#19, enabled by IE1 and reset when S#1 is read.
Reading S#1 returns the light pen or mouse flag, the identification number and FH, and resets FL and FH.
MAME clears only FH when S#1 is read and leaves FL as it was, where the book resets both flags.
While the mouse mode of R#8 is set, MAME ORs the two mouse buttons into bits 7 and 6 of S#1.
MAME raises FH at the horizontal interrupt line, takes the two mouse switches from its button state, and sets the identification bits at reset.
Status register 2 holds TR, VR, HR, BD, two 1 bits, EO and CE, from bit 7 to bit 0.
TR is the transfer ready flag, which the CPU checks while it transfers data.
VR is set while the vertical scanning is in progress.
HR is set while the horizontal scanning is in progress.
BD reports whether the search command detected the boundary color.
EO is 0 in the first field and 1 in the second.
CE reports that a command is being executed.
Reading S#2 returns the transfer ready flag, the scanning flags, the boundary and field flags and the command flag.
MAME fakes the horizontal scanning flag with a random bit on every read of S#2, and its own comment calls the earlier attempt nonsensical.
MAME raises the BD bit of S#2 when its search command meets the border color, and clears it when the search passes it.
MAME sets bit 6 of S#2, the vertical scanning flag, from one scanline of the frame to another.
MAME sets bit 7 of S#2 while a command has work left and clears it on a CPU transfer, the opposite of a transfer ready flag.
MAME clears bit 7 of S#2 when a command fetches or stores a value, and at reset.
MAME's drawing commands clear bit 0 of S#2, the command flag, as they finish.
MAME clears bit 0 of S#2 when a command is aborted or the mode changes.
MAME toggles bit 1 of S#2, the display field flag, at the vertical blanking.
Status register 3 is the low column register, whose eight bits are X7 to X0.
S#3 to S#6 give the collision location of the sprites, the light pen position and the mouse movement.
Reading S#3 returns the low eight bits of the column the collision, light pen or mouse reports.
While the mouse mode of R#8 is set, MAME returns the horizontal mouse delta from S#3 and clears it, not the stored register.
MAME adds each color bus count to the horizontal mouse delta and clamps the sum to 127 either way.
MAME's own TODO says S#3 to S#6 do not yet store the sprite collision, and its reset clears S#3, so it holds only that.
Status register 4 is the high column register: bits 7 to 1 are 1 and bit 0 is X8.
Bit 0 carries X8, the ninth bit of the column S#3 reports.
Reading S#4 returns the ninth bit of the column, X8, above seven 1 bits.
MAME's own TODO says S#3 to S#6 do not yet store the sprite collision, so X8 is never set and reads the 0 of the reset value.
Status register 5 is the low row register, whose eight bits are Y7 to Y0.
Reading S#5 returns the row register low, Y7 to Y0.
While the mouse mode of R#8 is set, MAME returns the vertical mouse delta from S#5 and clears it, not the stored register.
MAME adds each color bus count to the vertical mouse delta and clamps the sum to 127 either way.
MAME's own TODO says S#3 to S#6 do not yet store the sprite collision, and its reset clears S#5, so it holds only that.
Status register 6 is the high row register: bits 7 to 2 are 1, bit 1 is EO and bit 0 is Y8.
Bit 0 carries Y8 and bit 1 is EO, above six 1 bits.
Reading S#6 returns the ninth row bit, Y8, and the field flag above six 1 bits.
MAME's own TODO says S#3 to S#6 do not yet store the sprite collision, so Y8 is never set and reads the 0 of the reset value.
Status register 7 is the color register, whose eight bits are C7 to C0.
It holds the VRAM data of the POINT and VRAM to CPU commands.
Reading S#7 returns the VRAM data the last POINT or VRAM to CPU command fetched.
MAME also runs the pending command on the read and writes the value it returns into R#44, the command's own color.
MAME writes S#7 from every command engine and from a write to R#44, not only on the POINT and VRAM to CPU commands the book names.
Status register 8 is the low border X register, whose eight bits are BX7 to BX0.
When the search command detects the border color, the X coordinate is set in S#8 and S#9.
Reading S#8 returns the low eight bits of the X coordinate where the search command found the border color.
Status register 9 is the high border X register: bits 7 to 1 are 1 and bit 0 is BX8.
Bit 0 carries BX8, the ninth bit of the border X coordinate.
Reading S#9 returns the ninth bit of the border X coordinate, BX8, above seven 1 bits.
